chapter: Blue Devils, Moten and the Reno Club
title: Listening to Benny Goodman's and Fletcher Henderson's bands on the radio
summary: Basie says he listened to Goodman and Fletcher Henderson on Sunday night broadcasts, admired Goodman's polish and says the styles were different.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Were you listening to his records?
I used to hear him every Sunday night when he was playing from Chicago, you know. First he went on and then Fletcher Henderson came following him.
Oh, yeah?
I used to listen to them all night. (Inaudible) his records, Tommy Dorsey.
Did you like Benny's music?
Yes.
Why?
Because it was great.
How was it great?
Benny's band was swinging (inaudible). It was just marvelous.
Well, what was the difference between what he was doing and what you were doing?
He was playing a lot of music.
As opposed to?
He was playing a lot of music, good music. You know what I mean, they were there. You can't get away from that. They were there, for Christ's sake.
They were there?
Sure.
Compared to what you were doing though, at the time.
It's different.
How?
Well, I don't know. (Inaudible) different. It's different styles and different things like that. Benny was a very polished man.
Well, how did you feel about the polish?
I felt great about him, still do.
Why?
Because I do. I think he's wonderful. They were together.
Well, how was it that Benny Goodman polished different from Fletcher Henderson, whatever?
I don't know. I know Fletcher did a lot of arranging in that band, but never did sound alike.
Hm?
Well, they never sounded alike. But it's style (inaudible), you know, it was n't too different. Well, Fletcher, his band was very outstanding, great, (inaudible) marvelous. (Inaudible).
